name: What's the difference between a slow drain and a clogged drain?

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between a slow drain and a clogged drain?

acceptedAnswer.text: A slow drain means water eventually goes down, but at a significantly reduced rate. This usually indicates a partial blockage building up in the pipe. A clogged drain, on the other hand, means water is completely backed up and won't drain at all, suggesting a full obstruction. While a slow drain is often an early warning sign, both issues require attention to prevent further plumbing problems. Addressing a slow drain promptly can prevent it from becoming a full clog.
acceptedAnswer.description: A slow drain is a partial blockage where water drains slowly; a clogged drain is a full blockage where water doesn't drain at all.
